column3: The Hebrew says “at that time”; BSB says “at the regular time.”
The Hebrew says the matter was right in the eyes of the king and the assembly; BSB expresses this as pleasing them.
The Hebrew explicitly says the proclamation followed the king’s command; BSB introduces the words simply as what the letters read.
The Hebrew says “give a hand to the LORD”; BSB renders the image as “Submit to the LORD.”
The Hebrew says “the hand of God”; BSB says “the power of God.”
The Hebrew describes many people gathering and then calls them a very numerous assembly; BSB combines these descriptions.
The Hebrew says “the Passover” without explicitly specifying a lamb, which BSB supplies.
The Hebrew speaks of the purity of the holy place; BSB explicitly supplies “purification rules of the sanctuary.”
The Hebrew says Hezekiah spoke to the heart of the Levites and that they ate the festival; BSB says he encouraged them and they ate their assigned portion.
The Hebrew says their voice was heard, without naming the hearer; BSB explicitly names God.
